findings.title: Retry-count delete clause is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany `OR` has a second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. It deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. Only the SMS cron increments retryCount today, but the column is generic. Any future retry logic in other crons would be silently wiped by this job. The `method: SMS` condition should be applied to both branches, or moved outside the OR.

findings.title: Threshold `gt: 1` does not match the 'failed twice' description
findings.body: The deletion condition is `retryCount > 1`. A reminder is removed in the next cron run after its second failure, when retryCount becomes 2. That matches 'failed twice', but it is an off-by-one-prone magic number with no constant or comment. It also means a single transient Twilio error leaves only one more chance before the reminder is deleted. Define a named constant for the max retries.

findings.title: Catch block update can itself throw and abort the whole cron loop
findings.body: The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the `catch` is not guarded. If the update fails (DB error, or the row was deleted concurrently), the exception escapes the loop. The remaining reminders are not processed and the handler returns a 500. It should be wrapped in its own try/catch or use updateMany.

findings.title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message are never counted as failures
findings.body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. A reminder with a missing or invalid phone number (`sendTo` null) or an empty message is skipped without incrementing retryCount. It is re-evaluated on every cron run until its date passes, which is the exact behavior the PR aims to stop.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment
findings.body: The code writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` from a value read earlier. If two cron invocations overlap, both write the same value and an increment is lost. Use `{ increment: 1 }` instead.

findings.title: No tests for new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: The retry-count increment and the deletion of reminders after repeated failures are new behavior in a cron job and have no test coverage. The comment above the deleteMany is also now inaccurate, since it also deletes by retryCount.
